title: A Stacks-defined left derived value is a pointwise Kan-extension value
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal D'$ be categories, let $S$ be a right multiplicative system of arrows of $\mathcal D$ (Stacks Categories Definition Tag 04VC: (RMS1) identities lie in $S$ and $S$ is closed under composition; (RMS2) for $s:Y\to W$ in $S$ and any $f:Z\to W$ there are $t:V\to Z$ in $S$ and $g:V\to Y$ with $f\circ t=s\circ g$; (RMS3) if $f,g:X_1\to Y$ and $s\in S$ with source $Y$ satisfy $s\circ f=s\circ g$, then there is $t\in S$ with target $X_1$ and $f\circ t=g\circ t$), let $Q:\mathcal D\to S^{-1}\mathcal D$ be the localization of $\mathcal D$ at $S$ (the right localization, as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), and let $F:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ be a functor. (This covers Stacks Situation Tag 05S8, with $\mathcal D,\mathcal D'$ triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category] and $F$ exact, since the multiplicative system $S$ there is in particular a right multiplicative system.) Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal D$ and $Y$ an object of $\mathcal D'$. Let $S/X$ be the cofiltered category of arrows $s:X'\to X$ in $S$, with morphisms the commuting triangles (Stacks Remark Tag 05Q4). Suppose the left derived functor of $F$ is defined at $X$ with value $Y$ in the sense of Stacks Definition Tag 05S9, i.e. the pro-object $G:S/X\to\mathcal D'$, $(s:X'\to X)\mapsto F(X')$, is essentially constant with value $Y$ [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram], with cone $u_s:Y\to F(X')$. Then $F$ has a pointwise right Kan extension along $Q$ at $QX$ with value $Y$: the functor $(X',\varphi)\mapsto F(X')$ on the structured-arrow category of pairs $(X',\ \varphi:QX\to QX')$ (a morphism $(X',\varphi)\to(X'',\psi)$ being an arrow $a:X'\to X''$ of $\mathcal D$ with $Q(a)\circ\varphi=\psi$) has a limit, and it has a limit cone with vertex $Y$ whose projection at $(X',Q(s)^{-1})$ is $u_s$ for every object $s:X'\to X$ of $S/X$. In particular the projection at $(X,\mathrm{id}_{QX})$ is $u_{\mathrm{id}_X}:Y\to F(X)$, the canonical comparison map of Definition 05S9.

proof.text: The supplied retraction/factorization witness makes Cone.mk Y u a limit of the denominator diagram. For a cone v use v.app j0 followed by r as lift. For each j the common-stage factorization and naturality give the leg equation; the retraction equation proves uniqueness.

For a structured arrow j choose a right fraction a representing its structural map (Localization.exists_rightFraction). Define its leg as u at the denominator a.s followed by F.map a.f. This does not depend on the chosen representative: RightFraction.map_eq_iff gives a common refinement with equal denominators in W and equal numerators, and naturality of u identifies both composites. Applying this independence to the fraction with numerator a.f followed by the underlying arrow of a structured-arrow morphism proves naturality. For an inverse denominator use the identity numerator to obtain exactly the supplied leg.

Define the denominator-to-structured-arrow functor using inverse localized denominators. For any cone v on structured arrows, restrict v along this functor and take its unique lift through the denominator limit of Step 1. Every structured arrow receives a morphism from the inverse denominator of its representing fraction, with underlying arrow its numerator. Naturality of v along this morphism proves the lift equation. Uniqueness follows by restriction and the inverse-denominator leg equations. Thus the constructed cone is a limit. Package it as HasPointwiseRightKanExtensionAt, and use Localization.isoOfHom_id_inv for the identity-denominator comparison.
